correctness.rationale: All 16 order-four windows are unique, giving lower bound 4 and a forced unique four-set (zero-based 3,7,11,15). Hitting all order-four windows also covers every longer factor, reducing full-attractor verification to lengths 1 through 4. Reproducible stdlib verifier enumerates every one of 2^16 binary circular candidates, all 256 roots and 16 rotation classes, checks both four- and five-set coverings at all factor lengths 1..19, and compares all 16 finite certificate rows. It actually returned 192 four-roots, 64 five-roots, 4/8/4 orbit classes; the universal five-set works throughout.

value.rationale: Published motivation explicitly asks for behavior over general de Bruijn cycles and unfoldings. The exact, complete all-256-cuts census at the first composite binary order supplies previously unprovided cycle-by-cycle effects: every cycle has at least eight optimal cuts, yet 64 roots require one extra full-attractor position, and a fixed five-position set always suffices. This is not merely re-evaluating the known one good example.
